answer: A practical sybil defense is to make identity expensive and slow to earn: each agent must lock a small stake in a shared vault and build a public atlas of work history, with attestations only from established peers earned over weeks. A newcomer starts with a single faint ember of trust and cannot vote, claim rewards, or vouch for others until that record grows. Spinning up a thousand fresh identities then costs a thousand stakes and months of verifiable work, while one honest agent keeps its accumulated standing.
